titulo.en: Dear Madam: I'm writing to file a complaint

objetivo.en: Write a formal email with a greeting, a purpose, an attachment and a closing.

traduccion.en: the heading, the header

nota.en: Say “ehn-kah-beh-SAH-doh”: the z sounds like s and the d between vowels like the th in “this”. In an email it is the top part: who writes, who receives and the subject.

traduccion.en: the subject (line), the matter

nota.en: Say “ah-SOON-toh”. In an email, asunto is the subject line. Do not use it for a school subject; that is la materia.

traduccion.en: dear (in a formal greeting)

nota.en: Say “ehs-tee-MAH-doh”. It agrees with the person: Estimado señor, Estimada señora, Estimados señores. It is not “estimated”.

traduccion.en: to attach

nota.en: Say “ahd-hoon-TAR”: the j is a strong h. Adjunto la factura = I attach the invoice.

traduccion.en: the speed

nota.en: Say “beh-loh-see-DAHD”. The v sounds like a b, and the stress falls on the last syllable.

traduccion.en: the complaint, the claim

nota.en: Say “reh-klah-mah-SYOHN”. Presentar una reclamación = to file a complaint. It is not “reclamation”.

traduccion.en: the service

nota.en: Say “sehr-BEE-syoh”. Here it is the service you pay for, like internet or electricity.

traduccion.en: sincerely, yours truly

nota.en: A formal closing that goes before your name, followed by a comma: Atentamente, Emma García.

traduccion.en: the sender

nota.en: Say “reh-mee-TEHN-teh”. The remitente is the person who writes the email.

traduccion.en: to be waiting for (a reply)

nota.en: Quedo atento a su respuesta = I look forward to your reply. A woman says quedo atenta. Quedo is the yo form of quedar.

traduccion.en: the company, the business

nota.en: Say “ehm-PREH-sah”. Una empresa de internet = an internet company.

erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Estimados señores: Le escribo para presentar una reclamación.

explicacion.en: English speakers often open every email with “Hi”. In a formal email to a company use Estimados señores: with a colon, not Hola.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Le escribo por presentar una reclamación.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Le escribo para presentar una reclamación.

explicacion.en: English “to + verb” gives the purpose, so Spanish uses para + infinitive. Por would give a cause, not a purpose.

erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Estimada señora: Le escribo para solicitar información.

explicacion.en: English “Dear” never changes, but estimado agrees with the person: estimado señor, estimada señora.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Te escribo para solicitar información a la empresa.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Le escribo para solicitar información.

explicacion.en: A company gets usted, so the email says le and su, not te and tu. Use tú only with friends and family.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Quedo atento a su respuesta. Atentamente, Emma García
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Quedo atenta a su respuesta. Atentamente, Emma García

explicacion.en: The adjective agrees with the writer. Emma is a woman, so she writes quedo atenta; a man writes quedo atento.

titulo.en: The order of a formal email

texto.en: A formal email to a company follows a fixed order: greeting, purpose, a detail, what you attach and a closing. The greeting is Estimado señor: (to a man), Estimada señora: (to a woman) or Estimados señores: (to a company or several people). Estimado agrees with the person, and the greeting ends with a colon, not a comma. The purpose comes next: Le escribo para + infinitive, for example Le escribo para presentar una reclamación. Para + infinitive means “in order to”, so it answers “why am I writing?”. Other useful verbs are reclamar (to complain), solicitar (to request) and informar (to inform). Then give one clear detail, and say what you attach: Adjunto la factura (I attach the invoice).

titulo.en: Usted all the way, and the closing

texto.en: A company is not a friend, so the whole email uses usted: le (to you), su (your) and the usted form of the verb. Do not mix in te or tu. To ask for something, add por favor and the usted command: Por favor, revise el servicio (revise is the usted command of revisar, which you already know from the formal imperative). Close with Quedo atenta a su respuesta (a man writes atento) and then the word Atentamente, followed by a comma and your name. At the top, the encabezado shows the remitente (the sender) and the asunto (the subject line), for example: Asunto: Reclamación por la velocidad del servicio.
Choose your greeting and closing by the person you write to.

titulo.en: Would it be possible to change my card?

objetivo.en: Make very polite requests at the bank with ¿podría…?, ¿sería posible…? and le agradecería….

traduccion.en: the savings account

nota.en: Say “KWEHN-tah deh ah-OH-rrohs”. Ahorros comes from ahorrar (to save). The checking account is la cuenta corriente.

traduccion.en: the debit card

nota.en: Say “DEH-bee-toh” with the stress on the first syllable, which is why it has a written accent.

traduccion.en: the bank procedure, the bank errand

nota.en: Say “TRAH-mee-teh”. A trámite is any paperwork or errand at an office: forms, signatures, requests.

traduccion.en: the balance (of an account)

nota.en: Say “SAHL-doh”. El saldo de mi cuenta = my account balance.

traduccion.en: the branch (of a bank or a company)

nota.en: Say “soo-koor-SAHL”. The c in suc- sounds like k, and the stress falls on the last syllable.

traduccion.en: the ID document

nota.en: Say “ee-dehn-tee-DAHD”. It is the national ID card or the passport.

traduccion.en: the ATM

nota.en: Say “kah-HEH-roh”: the j is a strong h. A cajero is also a teller or cashier.

traduccion.en: to block, to freeze (a card)

nota.en: Say “bloh-keh-AR”. Se bloquea la tarjeta = the card gets blocked.

traduccion.en: the PIN, the secret code

nota.en: Say “KLAH-beh”: the v sounds like a b. Clave is also the password for an app.

traduccion.en: the statement (of an account)

nota.en: Say “ehks-TRAHK-toh”. El extracto lists what you spent and received. It is not “extract”.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: ¿Sería posible a recibir la tarjeta esta semana?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: ¿Sería posible recibir la tarjeta esta semana?

explicacion.en: English “possible to receive” makes learners add a. In Spanish the infinitive comes right after posible, with no a and no de.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Le agradecería ayudarme.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Le agradecería su ayuda.

explicacion.en: After le agradecería, use a noun: su ayuda, una respuesta. A verb needs a different structure that you will learn later.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: ¿Podrías firmar aquí, por favor?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: ¿Podría firmar aquí, por favor?

explicacion.en: With a bank executive you use usted, so the verb is podría. Podrías is tú and is for friends and family.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: ¿Podría me ayudar?
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: ¿Podría ayudarme?

explicacion.en: A pronoun cannot go between podría and the infinitive. Put it at the end of the infinitive (ayudarme) in one word.

titulo.en: Could you…? Would it be possible…?

texto.en: English softens a request with “could” or “would”: “Could you help me?”, “Would it be possible to…?”. Spanish does the same with the conditional. ¿Puede ayudarme? is already polite, but ¿Podría ayudarme? is more polite. Podría is the conditional of poder, and you use it with usted: ¿Podría firmar aquí, por favor? For a bigger request, use ¿Sería posible + infinitive?, which means “Would it be possible to…?”: ¿Sería posible recibir la tarjeta esta semana? Sería is the conditional of ser. Do not put a or de before the infinitive: posible recibir, not posible a recibir. These two openers fit a bank executive, a manager or anyone you address as usted.

To ask for something in writing or in person with great politeness, say Le agradecería + noun: Le agradecería su ayuda (I would appreciate your help), Le agradecería una respuesta. Le is usted, and agradecería is the conditional of agradecer (to be grateful for). After it, use a noun for now, not a verb. You already know another polite way to ask: Me gustaría una cuenta de ahorros. Direct forms like Quiero…, Necesito… and commands such as Muéstreme… sound blunt with a stranger, so soften them: Le agradecería el formulario instead of Necesito el formulario.
The same request in a blunt way and in a polite way.

objetivo.en: Ask for a refund at a store, explaining the cause (por) and the deadline or recipient (para).

traduccion.en: the refund, the reimbursement

nota.en: Say “reh-een-TEH-groh”. It is money paid back to you, like un reembolso.

traduccion.en: the system

nota.en: Say “sees-TEH-mah”. It is masculine even though it ends in -a: el sistema, un sistema nuevo.

traduccion.en: the acknowledgment of receipt

nota.en: Say “ah-KOO-seh deh reh-SEE-boh”. It is a paper or message that confirms something was received.

traduccion.en: the charge, the collection of a payment

nota.en: Say “KOH-broh”. Cobrar is the verb: me cobraron = they charged me.

traduccion.en: to refund, to pay back

nota.en: Say “reh-een-teh-GRAR”. Vamos a reintegrar el dinero = we are going to pay the money back.

traduccion.en: by mistake

nota.en: Say “pohr eh-RROR”: the rr in error is a trill.

traduccion.en: by (bank) transfer

nota.en: Say “trahns-feh-REHN-syah”. The c sounds like s.

traduccion.en: the garment, the piece of clothing

nota.en: Say “PREHN-dah”. Una prenda is any single piece of clothing, like a jacket or a shirt.

traduccion.en: the amount (of a payment)

nota.en: Say “eem-POR-teh”. It is not “import”: el importe is how much a charge or a payment is.

traduccion.en: the double charge

nota.en: Say “DOH-bleh KOH-broh”. It is when the same payment is charged twice.

erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Me cobraron dos veces por error.

explicacion.en: English “by mistake” gives no clue, and learners reach for para. A mistake is a cause, so Spanish uses por: por error.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Necesito el reembolso por el lunes.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Pagué 45 dólares para la chaqueta.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Pagué 45 dólares por la chaqueta.

explicacion.en: English “for” in “I paid $45 for the jacket” is a price or exchange, so Spanish uses por, not para.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Este comprobante es por usted.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Este comprobante es para usted.

explicacion.en: English “for you” can be por or para. When something is meant for a person (the recipient), use para: para usted.

titulo.en: Por: why, how and how much

texto.en: Por answers three questions: why, by what means and for how much. A cause: Me cobraron dos veces por error (They charged me twice by mistake) and Por eso vine a la tienda (That is why I came). A means: por correo, por teléfono, por transferencia (by mail, by phone, by transfer). A price or exchange: Pagué 45 dólares por la chaqueta (I paid 45 dollars for the jacket). A part of the day: por la mañana, por la tarde. You already know the basic uses of por and para; here you add these.

titulo.en: Para: by when, for whom and what for

texto.en: Para points forward. A deadline: Lo necesito para el lunes (I need it by Monday). A recipient: Este comprobante es para usted (This receipt is for you). A purpose, before an infinitive: Fui a la tienda para devolver la chaqueta (I went to the store to return the jacket). Compare Lo necesito para el lunes (a deadline) with Me lo cobraron por error (a cause). English “for” can be por or para, and English “by” can be por (by mail) or para (by Monday), so decide by the meaning, not by the English word.

titulo.en: One thousand two hundred fifty point fifty

objetivo.en: Read, write and say large and decimal amounts (mil, millón, 1.250,50) in a bank transaction.

traduccion.en: the decimal

nota.en: Say “deh-see-MAHL”. The c sounds like s. A decimal number has a comma: 12,50.

traduccion.en: the million

nota.en: Say “mee-YOHN”: ll sounds like the y in “yes”. Careful: un billón is a trillion; a billion is mil millones.

traduccion.en: the (bank) transfer

nota.en: Say “trahns-feh-REHN-syah”. Hacer una transferencia = to make a transfer.

traduccion.en: the amount, the quantity

nota.en: Say “kahn-tee-DAHD”. La cantidad is the number of dollars or things.

traduccion.en: the total amount (of money)

nota.en: Say “MOHN-toh”. In Latin America el monto is the total sum of a payment or a charge.

traduccion.en: the fee, the commission

nota.en: Say “koh-mee-SYOHN”. A bank charges una comisión for a service.

traduccion.en: to deposit

nota.en: Say “deh-poh-see-TAR”. Quiero depositar tres mil dólares.

traduccion.en: to withdraw (money)

nota.en: Say “reh-tee-RAR”. Retirar dinero del cajero = to take money out of the ATM.

traduccion.en: to save (money)

nota.en: Say “ah-oh-RRAR”: the h is silent and the rr is a trill.

traduccion.en: the cents

nota.en: Say “sehn-TAH-bohs”: the c sounds like s and the v like b. A dollar has cien centavos.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Quiero depositar un mil dólares.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Quiero depositar mil dólares.

explicacion.en: English says “one thousand”, so learners add un. In Spanish mil stands alone: mil dólares. Use a number before it only for more: dos mil.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: El edificio cuesta dos millón de dólares.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: El edificio cuesta dos millones de dólares.

explicacion.en: Millón is a noun, so it takes a plural after dos: dos millones (the accent disappears in the plural).

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Quiero ahorrar un millón dólares.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Quiero ahorrar un millón de dólares.

explicacion.en: After millón or millones you always need de before a noun: un millón de dólares. English has no “of” here.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: La transferencia es de mil y doscientos cincuenta dólares.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: La transferencia es de mil doscientos cincuenta dólares.

explicacion.en: The word y goes only between tens and units (treinta y cinco). Do not put y after mil or between hundreds.

texto.en: Mil is a single word that never changes and never takes un: mil dólares, dos mil dólares, cien mil dólares. After mil, say the hundreds directly, with no y: tres mil doscientos (3.200), doce mil quinientos (12.500). Millón behaves like a noun: un millón, dos millones, and it needs de before the thing counted: un millón de dólares, dos millones de dólares. The word y appears only between tens and units: setenta y cinco, sesenta y tres. Be careful with one false friend: un billón is a trillion (a million millions); “a billion” is mil millones.

titulo.en: Decimals and how to write them

texto.en: Spanish traditionally writes a point for the thousands and a comma for the decimals: 1.250,50, where English writes 1,250.50. You read the comma as con (or coma): mil doscientos cincuenta con cincuenta. For money, 12,50 is doce con cincuenta: dollars first, then cents (centavos). In Ecuador both styles are used: some receipts, apps and screens write 1,250.50 and others 1.250,50, so look at the context before you read. This lesson writes 1.250,50 and gives the English style in parentheses when it helps. A point inside a number is not a decimal: 2.000 is dos mil.

titulo.en: You'll receive your money within fifteen days

objetivo.en: Understand and set deadlines in a complaint: a partir de, dentro de, en un plazo de.

traduccion.en: the period of time, the span

nota.en: Say “LAHP-soh”. Un lapso de quince días = a span of fifteen days. It is close to plazo, but it is only the length of time.

traduccion.en: starting from, from… on

nota.en: Say it as one phrase: “ah pahr-TEER deh”. With el it becomes a partir del: a partir del lunes.

traduccion.en: in, within (counting from now)

nota.en: Say “DEHN-troh deh”. Dentro de dos días = two days from now.

traduccion.en: the adjustment, the correction

nota.en: Say “ah-HOOS-teh”: the j is a strong h. In billing, un ajuste corrects an amount.

traduccion.en: the overcharge

nota.en: Say it with the stress on KOH-broh. It is money charged above what you owe.

traduccion.en: the promise

nota.en: Say “proh-MEH-sah”. The verb is prometer: le prometo = I promise you.

traduccion.en: customer service

nota.en: Say “ah-tehn-SYOHN ahl klee-EHN-teh”. It is the department that answers customers.

traduccion.en: working, business (day)

nota.en: Say “AH-beel”: the h is silent and the stress is on the first syllable. Un día hábil is a business day, from Monday to Friday.

traduccion.en: to expire

nota.en: Say “ehks-pee-RAR”. La promesa expira el viernes = the promise expires on Friday.

traduccion.en: the deadline

nota.en: Say “FEH-chah LEE-mee-teh”. Stress the first syllable of límite.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: A partir de el lunes se corregirá la factura.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: A partir del lunes se corregirá la factura.

explicacion.en: English speakers often write each word separately. Spanish always joins de + el into del: a partir del lunes.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Dentro quince días recibirá su dinero.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Dentro de quince días recibirá su dinero.

explicacion.en: English “within fifteen days” has no small word to translate, but Spanish needs de: dentro de quince días.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: En un plazo quince días recibirá su dinero.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: En un plazo de quince días recibirá su dinero.

explicacion.en: Plazo is followed by de before the time: en un plazo de quince días, like “within a period of fifteen days”.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Yo recibirá el dinero dentro de dos días.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Yo recibiré el dinero dentro de dos días.

explicacion.en: In the future, yo ends in -é (recibiré) and usted, él and ella end in -á (recibirá). Emma talking about herself uses -é.

titulo.en: Three ways to set a deadline

texto.en: Complaints are full of dates. A partir de + a date or a moment means “starting from”: A partir del lunes se corregirá la factura (de + el becomes del). Dentro de + a length of time counts from now (you met dentro de ocho días earlier): Dentro de dos días viene el técnico means “two days from now”. En un plazo de + a length of time means “within a period of…” and is common in formal promises: En un plazo de quince días recibirá el reembolso. A plazo is the time allowed to do something, and a lapso is the span of time itself. When a plazo ends, it expira, and that day is la fecha límite (the deadline).

You already know the regular future. Companies promise with it: recibirá (you will receive), visitará (will visit), se corregirá (will be corrected), vendrá (will come). For usted, él and ella the regular future adds -á to the infinitive; for yo it adds -é (recibiré). Se corregirá la factura means “the invoice will be corrected” without saying who does it. In conversation you can also use ir a + infinitive: Voy a recibir el dinero. In deadlines, días hábiles are business days, from Monday to Friday, so diez días hábiles is two weeks. A plazo without hábiles counts every day.
Words you will meet in the examples and in the call.

contexto.en: Emma calls the customer service of her internet company again. She and the Operadora (the operator) use usted. The operator makes three promises with deadlines.

dialogo.texto: Atención al cliente, buenas tardes. ¿Cómo le puedo ayudar?

traduccion.en: Customer service, good afternoon. How can I help you?

dialogo.texto: Buenas tardes. Soy Emma García. Hace unos días escribí un correo por la velocidad del internet, pero todavía no tengo respuesta.

traduccion.en: Good afternoon. I'm Emma García. A few days ago I wrote an email about the speed of the internet, but I still have no answer.

dialogo.texto: Sí, veo su correo. Reconozco el problema y le pido disculpas. Le prometo tres cosas.

traduccion.en: Yes, I see your email. I acknowledge the problem and I apologize. I promise you three things.

dialogo.texto: Primero, dentro de cuarenta y ocho horas un técnico visitará su departamento. Segundo, a partir del lunes se corregirá la factura. Tercero, en un plazo de quince días recibirá la devolución del cobro de más.

traduccion.en: First, within forty-eight hours a technician will visit your apartment. Second, starting Monday the invoice will be corrected. Third, within fifteen days you will receive the refund of the overcharge.

dialogo.texto: Entonces el técnico viene dentro de dos días, la factura cambia a partir del lunes y recibo el dinero en un plazo de quince días. ¿Es correcto?

traduccion.en: So the technician comes in two days, the invoice changes from Monday and I receive the money within fifteen days. Is that correct?

dialogo.texto: Así es. Esa es la fecha límite de la empresa.

traduccion.en: That's right. That is the company's deadline.

dialogo.texto: Gracias. ¿Y cuánto cuesta la visita del técnico?

traduccion.en: Thank you. And how much does the technician's visit cost?

dialogo.texto: La visita del técnico es gratis. No hay ningún costo para usted.

traduccion.en: The technician's visit is free. There is no cost for you.

dialogo.texto: Muy bien. Le agradecería un correo con esta promesa, por favor.

traduccion.en: Very well. I would appreciate an email with this promise, please.

dialogo.texto: Claro. Le enviamos un mensaje hoy mismo con las tres promesas.

traduccion.en: Of course. We will send you a message today with the three promises.

dialogo.texto: Muchas gracias. Quedo atenta.

traduccion.en: Thank you very much. I look forward to it.

dialogo.texto: Gracias a usted. Hasta luego.

traduccion.en: Thank you. See you later.
